episodes.200273: Multiple days of thunderstorms across Central Alabama resulted in instances of wind damage and hail across the region from May 1-3. During the morning of May 1, a lightning strike in Pell City resulted in an injury. Wind damage and hail on May 2 was generally concentrated along and north of Interstate 59/20 as a line of severe thunderstorms moved from Mississippi to Georgia. A fatality and injury occurred the morning of May 3 near Red Mountain in Birmingham after a tree fell on power workers repairing damage from the previous evening. Wind damage and hail were less prevalent on the evening of May 3 as another line of thunderstorms moved southeastward across Central Alabama. However, a brief EF-0 tornado occurred in the Salem area of Lee County, causing minor tree damage.
episodes.200286: Isolated to scattered supercell thunderstorms developed ahead of complex of thunderstorms that formed along a pre-frontal trough axis approaching NW Alabama during the mid-day hours on May 2nd, 2025.  This activity continued to develop as this complex of thunderstorms formed into more than one line of strong to severe thunderstorms that pushed across northern Alabama during the mid to late afternoon hours. Numerous reports of wind damage were reported and hail up to golf ball size (especially in severe supercells that developed ahead of the line) occurred.
episodes.200326: A line of strong thunderstorms moved into northwestern Alabama  during the late morning hours along a pre-frontal trough axis ahead of an approaching cold front. As the line moved into central and eastern Alabama, portions of this line became severe producing damaging winds, especially in northeast Alabama.
episodes.200391: A passing cold front moves through southern New England bringing a line of storms which produced relatively widespread damaging winds, taking down trees and power lines in western/central MA and CT. Storms fizzled out as they reached RI and southeast MA.
episodes.200392: A passing cold front moves through southern New England bringing a line of storms which produced relatively widespread damaging winds, taking down trees and power lines in western/central MA and CT. Storms fizzled out as they reached RI and southeast MA.
episodes.200653: Several supercell thunderstorms and small thunderstorm clusters produced large hail and scattered damaging wind gusts. A few of the large hail and wind damage reports were considerable in nature.

episodes.201062: Strong to severe discrete thunderstorms were initiated along a slow moving frontal boundary in an area with about 1000 J/kg of SBCAPE. They were able to become somewhat organized given the 40 kt of effective bulk shear that was available due to a belt of southwesterly flow aloft. The storms produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.201063: Strong to severe discrete thunderstorms were initiated along a slow moving frontal boundary in an area with about 1000 J/kg of SBCAPE. They were able to become somewhat organized given the 40 kt of effective bulk shear that was available due to a belt of southwesterly flow aloft. The storms produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.201345: Isolated to scattered showers and storms developed over the western and southern portions of central North Carolina in the late afternoon and early evening. A more widespread cluster of storms developed over the southern Piedmont and tracked into the Triangle and Coastal Plain. These storms produced isolated wind damage in Montgomery and Richmond counties.
episodes.201560: An area of thunderstorms moved into eastern Tennessee during the afternoon hours on May 2, 2025. Damaging wind reports were seen throughout the Cumberland plateau and Tennessee valley, but the strongest storms and greatest concentration of severe weather reports were mainly in the southern Tennessee valley. Flash flooding, damaging winds, and even some severe sized hail were seen there.
episodes.201747: The weekend of the 3rd and 4th brought a closed upper low with much cooler and showery conditions, with highs only in the 50s for lower elevations and mid-upper 40s near the Sierra on the 4th. On the 3rd, scattered thunderstorms across northwest and west central NV produced brief heavy rainfall and gusty outflow winds.
episodes.201881: A slow moving cold front was the causing factor of showers and early afternoon thunderstorms across northwest Connecticut on Saturday, May 3, 2025. One linear convective system in particular became severe in strength, inflicting wind damage to trees and powerlines across central Litchfield County. Several reports were conveyed to NWS Albany of downed trees and wires blocking roadways and causing temporary closures.
episodes.201882: A slow moving cold front was the causing factor of showers and early afternoon thunderstorms across western Massachusetts on Saturday, May 3, 2025. A couple of these thunderstorms became severe in strength, inflicting wind damage to trees in Berkshire County. A few reports were conveyed to NWS Albany of downed trees blocking roadways and causing temporary closures.
episodes.201883: A slow moving cold front was the causing factor of showers and early afternoon thunderstorms across eastern New York on Saturday, May 3, 2025. While showers were more widespread throughout the region, thunderstorm activity became more concentrated within the Mid-Hudson Valley and Taconics where instability within the warm sector of the parent low pressure system rose more significantly. A couple of individual storms in the Mid-Hudson Valley achieved severe strength with 1 inch hail being reported. Another storm, a linear convective system, in particular also became severe in strength, inflicting wind damage to trees and powerlines across the lower Mid-Hudson Valley and Taconics. Several reports were conveyed to NWS Albany of downed trees and wires blocking roadways and causing temporary closures.
episodes.201910: A weak disturbance passing under the mid-level ridge across the central and northern Great Plains produced isolated strong to severe thunderstorms over the higher elevations of the Davis Mountains and Stockton Plateau.
episodes.201930: A closed upper low slowly moved into the Tennessee Valley with an associated surface cold front moving into the area during the late afternoon and into the evening. This sparked scattered convection in a modestly unstable environment, but solid deep layer shear and mid-level lapse rates yielded severe hail in Bamberg County.
episodes.201996: An upper-level trough from northern Ontario southwest to the central Plains was pushing southeast through the day, as a weak surface boundary lingered from the Missouri Bootheel northeast along the Ohio River. South of the boundary, MLCAPE was 1000-2000J/kg and the effective shear was 30-40kts. Mid-level lapse rates were poor, generally 6K/km or lower, while low-level lapse rates were 7-8K/km. Scattered storms were ongoing before sunrise over northeast Arkansas and far west Tennessee, and they steadily approached west Kentucky through the morning. One particularly strong storm produced a bow-echo as it approached Hazel in Calloway County just before 1000CST. The storm produced wind damage in the form of uprooted trees from Hazel to Murray. One tree fell onto a truck near Hazel, and another fell into a house in Murray. Although the storm weakened, it grew upscale into the afternoon as it moved east of the Land Between the Lakes. The larger line of storms produced sporadic wind gusts up to 50mph and hail up to the size of dimes, as it moved through Christian and Todd Counties and also Daviess County. Later on in the early evening, a weak mid-level disturbance helped to force some showers across west Kentucky. Two cold air funnels were reported, one with a shower near Hickman, and one that didn't even have a nearby shower west of Sturgis in Union County. There was no indication that either of the funnels reached the ground or caused any damage.
episodes.202070: Thunderstorms produced strong winds as they moved across Galveston Bay.
episodes.202165: Thunderstorms developed along a cold front that moved into South-Central Texas from the north. The airmass in the warm sector was unstable, with strong vertical wind shear and steep mid-level lapse rates. This combination led to storms poducing large hail and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.202392: Southwesterly flow ahead of a cold front across the Ohio Valley increased moisture across the Mid Atlantic, and some clearing allowed CAPE to increase to the 500 to 1000 J/kg range in the Piedmont and Southside. However, more cloud cover throughout the morning hindered destabilization somewhat, which limited coverage of storms to the Virginia Southside. Enough shear in the atmosphere did allow some storms to grow stronger, and resulted in some scattered wind damage.
episodes.202393: Southwesterly flow ahead of a cold front across the Ohio Valley increased moisture across the Mid Atlantic, and some clearing allowed CAPE to increase to the 500 to 1000 J/kg range in the Piedmont. However, more cloud cover throughout the morning hindered destabilization somewhat, which limited coverage of storms. Enough shear in the atmosphere did allow some storms to grow stronger, and resulted in some scattered wind damage.
episodes.202426: Very heavy rainfall during the latter portions of April 2025 resulted in prolonged river flooding across portions of central and southern Oklahoma during the first days of May 2025.
episodes.202444: A cold front moved through the region in early May, bringing isolated severe thunderstorms and flooding.
episodes.202485: Widespread thunderstorm activity developed ahead of an approaching cold front. A disturbance moving across the western Gulf in the morning enhanced storm intensities which resulted in scattered wind damage reports northwest of Baton Rouge. Then, later in the day, a storm along the actual cold front spun off a weak tornado in the New Orleans area.
episodes.202486: A weak cold front moved through the local area on May 3rd. Marginal shear combined with sufficient instability resulted in a few severe thunderstorms along the coastal areas, including one waterspout.
episodes.202546: A mesoscale convective vortex moved across the Lower Mississippi Valley during the early morning hours. A second area of convection developed over Central Arkansas and approached the Mid-South during the late morning to early afternoon. Surface-based instability flourished across the region along with supportive shear and steep lapse rates, resulting in damaging winds and large hail across north Mississippi.
episodes.202565: A cold front moved into the mid-Mississippi Valley during the morning of May 2nd, with a line of showers and thunderstorms developing ahead of the front. Within the warm, humid air mass ahead of the front, temperatures warmed into the upper 70s by the early afternoon hours, allowing for 1500-2000 J/kg of MLCAPE to develop. Wind shear was fairly modest for the time of year, with between 25 and 30 kt of effective bulk shear present. As the line of storms moved across central Kentucky, a couple bowing segments developed, producing scattered wind damage along the Ohio River. An isolated stronger cell across south central Kentucky produced severe hail up to golf ball size, in addition to gusty winds.||The following morning on May 3rd, the cold front was still slowly pushing east across the area. While mostly light to moderate rain showers were present, one stronger cell was able to produce a brief EF0 tornado over Franklin County.
episodes.202720: An upper level trough traversed east across the Southern Plains on May 2nd, which reinforced a weak cold front southeast into portions of extreme Northeast Texas and Southwest Arkansas along the I-30 corridor by afternoon. Strong daytime heating contributed to ample air mass destabilization through the day across the warm and moist sector ahead of the front, with scattered severe thunderstorms developing by midday through much of the afternoon across East Texas. These storms produced sporadic reports of damaging winds, with locally heavy rainfall atop already saturated grounds resulting in flash flooding across portions of the region as well. While the severe threat diminished by mid afternoon, flash flooding persisted through the evening hours.
episodes.202819: A quasi-linear convective system moved across northwest Georgia during the afternoon and evening hours of May 2nd along a modest cold front. Winds damage and some hail were the main threats, however conditions became less conducive to severe weather south and east of I85. Complex outflow interactions along the edge of one of the northern embedded cells managed to produce a brief EF1 tornado which crossed Lake Lanier. The lowest radar scan was above the strong rotation signature.
episodes.202821: A QLCS moved through North and Central Georgia in the afternoon and evening hours of the 3rd. The line initially posed a robust wind threat with measured wind gusts of near 70 mph. As the line moved across central Georgia cells in the warm sector merged with the line initiating numerous quick spin-up tornadoes and requiring at least 10 tornado warnings. Many of the rotational signatures were shallow and only visible from the TATL radar.
episodes.202902: A weak shortwave trough, coupled with ample instability, supportive shear and lapse rates, helped drive a broken line of severe thunderstorms across southwestern North Carolina, delivering damaging winds to the two counties.
episodes.203117: A strong low pressure system persisted around the region for several days, helping to fuel thunderstorms. Several storms produced severe weather and flash flooding.

episodes.203700: Unstable and wet weather conditions were anticipated in early May due to a combination of abundant tropical moisture and a series of upper-level troughs moving over the region.
